# Uber current public homepage — October 5, 2026

## Evidence and composition
Reference https://www.uber.com/ca/en/ as rendered in the browser, in English. The independent HTTP request returned 406; preserve that failure. The visible city label was Taipei, CA, a dated public geographic variant, not a live location calculation.

## Typography and color
Use original UberMove Bold/Regular and UberMoveText Medium/Regular fonts from the official tb-static.uber.com CDN. Black top navigation, white canvas, gray input and service tiles, bold black headings and compact black buttons. Desktop h1 is 52px/64px at weight700; desktop h2 is 36px/44px. Mobile h1 is 36px/44px, h2 is 28px/36px. Main text is 16px/24px.

## Desktop geometry
At 1280×720 the black header is 64px high. The content has 64px side padding and a 1152px width. The hero is a two-column layout: a 459px text/form column at x64, and the original 459px square essentials/luggage illustration at x658/y128. The heading begins x64/y160 and wraps over 128px. Include the city row, Pickup now pill, pickup and dropoff fields, See prices, login link, and the image's original Ready to travel / Schedule ahead overlay. Explore what you can do starts y651, with five light service tiles. Account, Reserve, City Hub, driving, business and app-download sections follow, then the complete black footer.

## Mobile geometry
At 390×844 the header stays 64px high. Use 24px margins, a 342px content width, and a compact login/signup/menu header. The city row precedes h1 at x24/y136. Hide the desktop hero illustration and Pickup now pill. Keep two 56px fields, the See prices button and separate login link. Explore heading starts y560, followed by two larger Ride/Reserve tiles and three smaller Courier/Food/Grocery tiles. Stack the remaining source sections, with original source artwork and the full footer.

## Review boundary
This is an unofficial visual study. Editable fields and local controls must not request geolocation, submit rides, accept financial commitments or invent fare estimates. External service actions point to the genuine official service. Preserve the dated source differences and do not claim responsive or visual parity before testing.
